chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Awn al-Qalanisi, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The one who meets the Muslims with two faces and two tongues will come on the Day of Judgment and for him will be two tongues of Fire.

key_terms.لِسَانَانِ مِنْ نَارٍ: two tongues of fire (punishment for deceit)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of being two-faced towards Muslims according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the 'two-tongued' individual as one whose external demeanor and speech shift to suit different audiences, a condition of spiritual hypocrisy. The punishment of literal 'tongues of fire' serves as a *muthul* (symbolic correspondence), where the organ of deceit becomes the instrument of eternal torment, emphasizing the severity of insincerity in Shia ethical tradition. This concept is often linked to the broader theme of *riya'* (showing off) and the loss of inner consistency.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Awn Al Qalanasy, from Ibn Abu Yafour, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who meets the Muslims by two faces and two tongues would come on the Day of Judgment and for him would be two tongues of Fire’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ‘Awn al-Qalanisi from ibn abu Ya’fur from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever meets the Muslims with two faces and tongues, he on the Day of Judgment will be raised with two tongues of fire.”
